subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class Docker `openclaw instance create/list/delete/update` commands, or should multi-instance Docker remain a documented manual Compose/profile workflow plus external wrapper territory for now?
rationale: The request would add official operator UX and persistence/update/delete semantics across Docker, config/state/workspace roots, ports, Compose names, cleanup, and sandbox boundaries; current source and docs do not provide a narrow cleanup-sized implementation to apply automatically.

options.title: Sponsor minimal core lifecycle
options.body: Approve a small explicit core design for named Docker instances, including identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

options.title: Keep manual primitives
options.body: Leave the current multi-gateway docs, environment variables, Docker setup script, and ClawDock helpers as the supported core path while tracking the product request.

options.title: Route to external wrapper
options.body: Decline core ownership unless a missing core API is identified, and ask contributors to maintain a wrapper or ClawHub package around the current primitives.

recommendation.title: Sponsor minimal core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve a small explicit core design for named Docker instances, including identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is ownership of the multi-gateway guide and profile-aware service naming that set the current product boundary.
